description: prisma's classification against the conformance corpus (conformance/actions.json). 'adapterUnsupported' lists 'conformance' actions this adapter cannot express, each with the reason (naming the real mechanism) and the substring its thrown error must contain. 'adapterSupportedExpected' lists 'expectedUnsupported' actions this adapter deliberately translates, so they are oracle-compared instead of thrown. 'expectedUnsupportedMessages' pins the throw message for every 'expectedUnsupported' action it does not promote, and 'nullRepresentationOmittedMessages' for every 'nullRepresentationOmitted' action. validate-corpus.sh checks all four against the corpus; the harness refuses to run with a message missing.

adapterUnsupported.reason: A backslash is a LIKE metacharacter on some providers and not others, so the same needle cannot mean the same thing on all of them: SQLite's LIKE has no escape character and matches a backslash literally, while PostgreSQL and MySQL treat it as the DEFAULT escape character with no ESCAPE clause present. endsWith('\\') is then a pattern ending in an escape character, which PostgreSQL rejects outright (SQLSTATE 22025), and a backslash anywhere inside a needle silently escapes the next character so contains('a\\b') would match 'ab' — a row the PDP denies.
